121	that I was already bereaved of the 12 tribes I was supposed to bring. In principle she was supposed to bring the 12
122	tribes. So why did she lose that? "I was bereaved of the 12 tribes too,
123	which I was supposed to bring, and now of both of you in one day." That is why it says "also," this one and that one.
124	See, poor Rivka. Now I don't understand: so he tore out her womb, so what? So what, he tore out
125	her womb? Can't HaShem make her another womb?
126	Didn't we see this about a womb? Sarai was barren, "she had no child."
127	The Gemara said: is it that a barren woman "has no child"?
128	Tractate Yevamot 65b: no, she did not even have a womb.
129	What did HaShem do?
130	He carved her a womb.
131	So what if Esav tore out her womb?
132	HaShem will carve her a new womb.
133	It is written like this about Ruth too.
134	Ruth had no womb, so the Midrash says, and HaShem carved her a womb.
135	So what is the problem?
136	But one who already gave birth, HaShem will not do a miracle for her now.
137	One who has not yet given birth, then He does, poor thing.
138	How does Rachel put it?
139	"Give me children, and if not, I am dead."
140	From here the Gemara learns, Nedarim 64b, and also in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetzé, Zohar Bereshit,
141	that a person who has no children is considered dead.
142	A woman who has no children, how does Chana put it, in Berachot 31b?
143	"These breasts that You gave me, why?"
144	"HaShem, Elokei Tzevaot, of all the hosts You created in the world, is it hard in Your eyes to give me one child? If You give
145	me a son, good; and if not, I will go and secede from Elkana my husband, and You will make Your Torah a forgery. He will suspect me
146	and make me drink the bitter waters. And You said that if she is barren, she will bear children: if dark,
147	she bears fair ones; if short, she bears tall ones." So first of all, whoever is dark, it implies from here, if dark, it implies
148	Sephardim, as opposed to the fair ones, so it implies. "If dark, she bears fair." What is
149	the simple meaning?
150	If a Sephardi woman gives birth, an Ashkenazi will be born?
151	That is not the simple meaning at all. What, do you think skin color decides?
152	What, do you think Rachel was fair-skinned?
153	From Baghdad, Aram Naharayim: Rachel, Leah, all the holy Patriarchs were all Iraqis.
154	What were they, Polish?
155	We never knew any Poland.
156	So what is "if dark, she bears fair"?
157	Every person is born with a ledger. What is written in his ledger?
158	If nothing is written and he is clean of sins from a previous incarnation, in this incarnation life will go well for him.
